text:
Dear Dr. Higgins,

Thank you for agreeing to evaluate this young girl. Her parents first noted a failure to maintain her expected linear and ponderal growth trajectories around twelve months of age, with progressive growth deceleration since that time.

Her neonatal course was completely uncomplicated, notably without any jaundice in the newborn period. Her appetite has always remained excellent without poor feeding, and her motor milestones have progressed normally. On examination, she is alert and comfortable. Vital signs are normal for age, and her heart and lung sounds are clear. Her abdomen is flat and soft with no detectable peritoneal fluid, and she has no generalized fluid retention or peripheral swelling.

Serum chemistry revealed a non-anion gap acidemia characterized by elevated circulating chloride and a depressed serum bicarbonate of 13 mmol/L, along with a low potassium level of 2.8 mmol/L. Circulating creatinine levels have been repeatedly normal. Despite profound systemic acidemia, her spot urine samples have stayed inappropriately alkaline with a pH above 7.0, demonstrating a failure of distal urinary acidification consistent with a classic distal tubular defect in acid secretion. A renal ultrasound demonstrated diffuse bilateral medullary calcium deposition.

Hematologic evaluation revealed active red blood cell destruction with dropped hemoglobin, low haptoglobin, and an elevated reticulocyte percentage of 6.2%. The red blood cells exhibited a reduced mean cell volume of 67 fL. Peripheral smear microscopy highlighted prominent polychromatophilic red cells alongside numerous erythrocytes with mouth-like or slit-shaped central pallor.

We have initiated potassium citrate supplementation, which she is tolerating well. I would be very grateful for your comprehensive assessment and recommendations regarding her combined renal and red cell abnormalities.

Sincerely,
Dr. Marcus Bell
